rules.statement: Never key behavior, metric attributes or audit fields off free-form, operator-supplied text such as a display name; use it for display only and select behavior or label telemetry with a registered, bounded vocabulary value.
rules.why: Arbitrary text can't safely select guardrails, and as a telemetry dimension its cardinality is unbounded. Registration is what keeps the set of values bounded.
rules.check: Look for branches, switch cases, metric tags or audit fields that read a free-form name or label setting rather than a registered type name or constant.

rules.statement: When a missing declaration selects security guardrails, the default must be the strictest choice (fail closed), so a forgotten setting never drops protections.
rules.why: A permissive default such as `development` fails open: one forgotten declaration silently removes the guardrails from a tenant that serves real users.
rules.check: Look at the default values of new settings or enums that turn on security restrictions or deletion protection. Flag any default that picks the permissive option when nothing is declared.

rules.statement: Let a package add a vocabulary value by registering a DI strategy class resolved through a catalog, not by editing a hard-coded list, and have the catalog reject empty names, duplicate names and references to unregistered entries when it is composed.
rules.why: Vocabularies are open unless provably closed. Validating when the catalog is composed makes a bad registration fail at startup instead of when data is first read.
rules.check: Look for new vocabulary types added as closed enums or switch statements instead of registered strategies. Check that a new catalog validates its names and cross-references when it is constructed, not lazily on lookup.

rules.statement: When a startup validator refuses non-production settings in the Production host environment, judge each registered value by its own declared flag (such as `IsProduction`) instead of comparing it against hard-coded names.
rules.why: The registered types decide, so a type contributed by another package is judged correctly without the validator having to know about it.
rules.check: In production-safety validators, look for string comparisons against built-in type names where the registered type's own flag should be read.

rules.statement: Stamp context that every audit or telemetry event needs (such as a tenant's effective type) once in the shared recorder, resolved once per entity per request, rather than passing it from each handler.
rules.why: If dozens of call sites each have to remember to pass the value, some will forget. Resolving it in the recorder stamps every event that names the entity.
rules.check: Look for new audit or telemetry fields that are threaded through individual handlers or endpoint call sites instead of being resolved centrally in the recorder.

rules.statement: In a management list or read response, add best-effort derived fields from stored settings only after authorization, and omit the field rather than failing the request when the stored settings are unreadable or name an unregistered value.
rules.why: The operator needs the list to find the broken resource and repair it, so one bad derived field must not hide the whole response.
rules.check: Look for new enrichment fields in management resources that throw or answer 409 when stored data is invalid, or that are computed before the authorization check.
